question: Which filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw standardize for this issue, and should exec path access be covered in the first version or split to a separate policy surface?
rationale: This defines a public config and local filesystem security boundary with competing open PR designs, upgrade risks, and an explicit exec-scope tradeoff, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Converge on `tools.fs` v1
options.body: Adopt one file/media/apply_patch policy model now, document or split exec scope, and require upgrade/security proof before merge.

options.title: Fold into security profile
options.body: Keep this issue as design input for the broader security-profile work and avoid adding a narrow config surface until the data-security model is chosen.

options.title: Stay with workspace-only
options.body: Decline allow/deny or roots config for now and rely on `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, tool allow/deny, Docker/OS isolation, and separate exec hardening work.

recommendation.title: Converge on `tools.fs` v1
recommendation.body: Adopt one file/media/apply_patch policy model now, document or split exec scope, and require upgrade/security proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest current issue-review and recent filesystem-policy history signal for choosing the security/config boundary.
